holidays.name: National Crab Rangoon Day
holidays.description: Today is for the crispy, creamy, golden-fried wonton triangles stuffed with cream cheese and imitation crab. They are a staple of American Chinese takeout. Grab a pile, dunk them in sweet chili sauce, and call it a balanced meal.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. The dish is usually linked to American tiki-style restaurants in the mid-20th century. Trader Vic's in California is often credited with popularizing it.
holidays.funFact: Cream cheese is a very American ingredient, and it is rarely found in traditional Chinese cooking. That makes crab rangoon a classic American-born creation, despite the name referencing Rangoon, Myanmar.

holidays.name: National Tortellini Day
holidays.description: This is a day to celebrate the small ring-shaped stuffed pasta, which is usually filled with cheese or meat. You can serve it in broth, tossed in cream sauce, or straight from the pot when nobody is looking.
holidays.origin: Tortellini comes from Emilia-Romagna in Italy, where Bologna and Modena both claim it. The day itself is an unofficial food observance. Its date near Valentine's Day suits a pasta with such a romantic legend.
holidays.funFact: Legend says tortellini was inspired by the navel of Venus, the goddess of love. A smitten innkeeper supposedly peeked through a keyhole and then shaped pasta to match what he saw.

holidays.name: Kiss Day
holidays.description: Kiss Day is a lovey-dovey pre-Valentine's observance. Couples mark it with kisses, whether a sweet peck on the cheek or something more dramatic. It is the sixth day of the Valentine's Week countdown.
holidays.origin: Kiss Day is an unofficial observance that grew out of the Valentine's Week tradition, popular in India and elsewhere in South Asia. Each day of the week from February 7 to 14 has its own theme, such as Rose Day or Hug Day. Kiss Day comes the day before Valentine's Day.
holidays.funFact: Valentine's Week days run in a set order: Rose, Propose, Chocolate, Teddy, Promise, Hug, Kiss, and then Valentine's Day. Kiss Day is the last warm-up before the main event.
